label: Men-at-arms of base type
summary: Whether the army has the given number of men-at-arms regiments of one base type.
details: The base type is written after a colon, as in `army.army_number_maa_regiments_of_base_type:archers`. Compare the count with <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Works on an army.

label: Men-at-arms of type
summary: Whether the army has the given number of men-at-arms regiments of one specific type.
details: The type is written after a colon, as in `army.army_number_maa_regiments_of_type:crossbowmen`. Compare the count with <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Works on an army.

label: Army size
summary: Whether the army's size compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla compares it with plain numbers such as `>= 3000` and `>= 4000`, and once with a script value. Works on an army.

label: Army supply
summary: Compares a number tied to the army's supply with another number; the game does not say more.
details: The game's documentation text asks "Can we disband this army?", which does not fit a number comparison, so the text does not describe the key. The meaning given here rests on the name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Artifact durability
summary: Whether the artifact's durability compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla mostly checks for low durability, for example `<= define:NInventory|ARTIFACT_LOW_DURABILITY` (a value set in the game's defines) or plain numbers such as `< 50`. Works on an artifact.

label: Artifact max durability
summary: Whether the artifact's maximum durability compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla compares it with the game's default maximum durability (`define:NInventory|ARTIFACT_DEFAULT_MAX_DURABILITY`), using `>=` and `<`. Works on an artifact.

label: Artifact slot type
summary: Whether the artifact is of the given inventory slot type.
details: Vanilla uses slot types such as `primary_armament`, `helmet`, `regalia`, `armor`, `book` and `throne`. Works on an artifact.

label: Artifact type
summary: Whether the artifact is of the given type.
details: Vanilla uses types such as `book`, `tapestry`, `chest`, `cabinet`, `animal_hide` and `throne`. Works on an artifact.

label: Assert if
summary: A debugging check that causes an assert while the game runs when its condition is true.
details: Vanilla uses it inside a script helper, with a message saying that a required scope is empty or missing. The message text is optional.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: The conditions that, when true, cause the assert.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The message shown with the assert.

label: Assert at read time
summary: A debugging check that causes an assert when the game reads the script.
details: It is written `assert_read = yes`, or with the message to print as a string. The game gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Attacker war score
summary: Whether the attacker's war score compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla uses values like `>= 90`, `<= -50` or a named value, so it can be negative. Works on a war.

label: Attraction
summary: Whether the character's attraction value compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla compares it with plain numbers (`>= 50`, `> 0`, `< 0`) and with named values such as `medium_positive_attraction`. It can be negative. Works on a character.

label: Auto-add rulers
summary: Whether the group automatically checks region rulers as possible participants.
details: If it is off, only characters added by hand can join the group. Written `yes` or `no`. Works on a situation participant group, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Available loot
summary: Whether the gold in the province that raiding or bartering armies can loot compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla uses `>= 5`. Works on a province.

label: Free taxpayer slots
summary: Whether the number of available taxpayer slots in the tax slot compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a tax slot. The documented example spells the key differently (`available_tax_player_slots`), so write it as listed here. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Average amenity level
summary: Whether the average amenity level of the character compares in the given way to a number.
details: The average is usually a decimal number, so checking for exact equality is rarely useful. Use a comparison such as `>= 3`. Works on a character.

label: Average faction opinion
summary: Whether the average opinion of the characters of the faction compares in the given way to a number.
details: The game's documentation does not say whom the opinion is held of. Works on a faction. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Faction opinion, not powerful vassals
summary: Whether the average opinion of the faction's characters who are not powerful vassals compares in the given way to a number.
details: Like the plain average faction opinion, but it leaves out powerful vassals. Works on a faction.

label: Faction opinion, powerful vassals
summary: Whether the average opinion of the faction's powerful vassals compares in the given way to a number.
details: Like the plain average faction opinion, but it counts only powerful vassals. Works on a faction.

label: Barter goods
summary: Whether the character has barter goods that compare in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla uses it both as a plain comparison (`> 0`) and once as a block with the fields `value` and `multiply`. The game does not document how the two combine. Works on a character.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The amount of barter goods to compare with; vanilla writes `50`.

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: A second value that vanilla gives next to `value`; the game does not document it.

label: Barter loot carried
summary: Whether the barter loot the army is carrying compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on an army. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Inspiration base gold cost
summary: Whether the inspiration's base gold cost compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on an inspiration. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Base weight
summary: Whether the character's base weight compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla does not use it, and the game does not say what unit the weight is in.

label: Birth date
summary: Whether the character's birth date, one number counting days since the first of January in year 0, compares in the given way to another number.
details: Because the date is one number, two characters can be compared directly, for example `scope:a.birth_date > scope:b.birth_date` (a was born later than b). Vanilla uses it once, comparing with another character's birth date. Works on a character.

label: Blood legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the lifestyle compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation does not say which lifestyle it means, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Levies from buildings
summary: Whether the levies a county or province gets from its buildings compare in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a title (a county) or a province. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Garrison from buildings
summary: Whether the maximum garrison a county or province gets from its buildings compares in the given way to a number.
details: Works on a title (a county) or a province. The documented example reads `levies > 100`, which does not match the key; the key itself is about the garrison.

label: Building slots
summary: Whether the number of building slots in the province, occupied ones included, compares in the given way to a number.
details: Vanilla uses values such as `<= 5`, `>= 1` and `<= 0`. Works on a province.

label: At least N true
summary: Whether the given number of the triggers inside it are true.
details: List the triggers in the block and set `amount`. Vanilla usually writes `amount >= 2`, which means at least two of them; it also writes a plain number (`amount = 2`), and the game does not say whether that means exactly or at least. Vanilla puts traits, perks, `OR` blocks and other triggers inside.

fields.name: amount
fields.text: How many of the triggers must be true.
fields.values: a number, or a comparison such as `>= 2`

fields.name: triggers
fields.values: any triggers, written one after the other

label: Can accept task contract
summary: Whether the character meets the requirements to accept the given task contract.
details: Write the contract after the equals sign, for example `can_accept_task_contract = scope:task_contract`. Works on a character. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Can add hook
summary: Whether trying to hook the target character would override the hook the character currently has on them.
details: If there is no current hook, it is always true. The duration is optional; without it the hook type's own duration is used. Vanilla mostly checks `favor_hook`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character who would be hooked.

fields.name: days / months / years
fields.text: How long the hook would last.

label: Can afford treasury budget
summary: Whether the character can pay the costs of the current treasury enact budget.
details: Written `yes` or `no`. Works on a character. Vanilla uses it once, with `yes`.

label: Can appoint for title
summary: Whether the character can be appointed for the given title.
details: The game's documentation says appointment is only allowed for the main administrative tier of the holder's government and above, and only when it is the holder's top-tier title. Vanilla gives it a title such as `root.primary_title`.

label: Can arrive in time
summary: Whether the character can arrive at the given activity in time.
details: The game says it is only a rough check, kept simple to be cheap to run. Write the activity after the equals sign, as vanilla does with `scope:activity`.

label: Can assign to tax slot
summary: Whether the character is valid to be assigned to the given tax slot.
details: Write the tax slot after the equals sign, for example `can_assign_to_tax_slot = scope:tax_slot`. Works on a character. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Can attack in hierarchy
summary: Whether the given character can be the attacker against the defender, judging by their liege and vassal relations.
details: Write the character after the equals sign. Vanilla uses it once, with a saved scope called `defender_check`. The game's documentation does not say who the defender is or which relations count.

label: Can be acclaimed
summary: Whether the character could become the Acclaimed Knight of an accolade.
details: Written `yes` or `no`. Works on a character. Vanilla always checks it with `yes`.

label: Can be child of
summary: Whether the given character was old enough to have children when the scoped character was born.
details: Only age is taken into account. Write the possible parent after the equals sign. Works on a character.

label: Can be claimed by
summary: Whether the given character can claim the artifact.
details: Write the character after the equals sign. Vanilla gives it saved scopes such as `scope:actor` or `scope:recipient`. Works on an artifact.

label: Can be employed as
summary: Whether the character can be employed in the given court position.
details: Vanilla names court positions such as `travel_leader_court_position`, `court_astrologer_court_position` and `wet_nurse_court_position`. Works on a character.
